LESSON: IMITATION

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.1: Imitation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Imitation. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: how, when and to?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate vocabulary to express self in different contexts
2. respond confidently to communication in different contexts
3. exhibit appropriate mannerisms during conversation in different contexts Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and Collaboration: learners practice conversation in pairs and groups Learning to learn: learners ask parents/guardians about mannerisms when communicating with adults

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. use appropriate vocabulary to express self in different contexts
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to use appropriate vocabulary to express self in different contexts. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. respond confidently to communication in different contexts
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to respond confidently to communication in different contexts. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. exhibit appropriate mannerisms during conversation in different contexts Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and Collaboration: learners practice conversation in pairs and groups Learning to learn: learners ask parents/guardians about mannerisms when communicating with adults
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to exhibit appropriate mannerisms during conversation in different contexts Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and Collaboration: learners practice conversation in pairs and groups Learning to learn: learners ask parents/guardians about mannerisms when communicating with adults. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Imitation using something you see at school.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Imitation.
2. Explain Imitation to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Imitation.
4. Show that you can: use appropriate vocabulary to express self in different contexts
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Imitation. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: how, when and to?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. use appropriate vocabulary to express self in different contexts
2. respond confidently to communication in different contexts
3. exhibit appropriate mannerisms during conversation in different contexts Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and Collaboration: learners practice conversation in pairs and groups Learning to learn: learners ask parents/guardians about mannerisms when communicating with adults

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
